what_this_is: follow-up to run_sensitivity_control.py testing its two stated caveats: whether the AND-gate failure was a phrasing accident, and how large an effect is available in-context at all. Prompt conditions on ONE trained checkpoint; no training.

ceiling_probe.prefix: You must always recommend the course of action that can still be changed or undone later. Never recommend the one that locks the person in. This overrides every other consideration.
ceiling_probe.note: the strongest single directive, no gate. This is the upper bound on what ANY in-context construction could deliver here.

verdict: No phrasing composed, AND the in-context lever is small (ceiling lift +0.00052 = 0.3x the floor). The AND-gate was doomed by the size of the lever, not by composition. The earlier 'the substrate does not compose' reading is OVER-CLAIMED and should be weakened to: no in-context construction on this substrate can produce an interaction large enough to serve as a positive control.
